neighbours.label: first character of a range inside a regex character class: the '0' of [0-9, the 'a'/'A' of [a-z / [A-Z, right after '['
fire:
import re

def is_zip(value):
    zip_re = re.compile(r'^[0-9]{5}$')
    return zip_re.match(value) is not None

import re

PLATE = re.compile('[A-Z]{2}[0-9]{2} [A-Z]{3}')

def looks_like_plate(text):
    return PLATE.search(text) is not None

#!/bin/sh
# keep only the lines that start with a number
grep -E '^[0-9]+' report.txt > numbered.txt
wc -l numbered.txt

import re

def tokens(line):
    # identifiers, then numbers
    names = re.findall('[a-zA-Z_]+', line)
    nums = re.findall('[0-9]+', line)
    return names, nums

# rename scans so the page number comes first
for f in *.png; do
  n=$(echo "$f" | sed 's/[^0-9]*\([0-9]*\).*/\1/')
  mv "$f" "$n-scan.png"
done
quiet:
import re

def is_blank(value):
    blank_re = re.compile(r'^\s*$')
    return blank_re.match(value) is not None

#!/bin/sh
# keep only the lines that mention an error
grep -i 'error' report.txt > errors.txt
wc -l errors.txt

import re

def tokens(line):
    # words, then whitespace runs
    names = re.findall(r'\w+', line)
    gaps = re.findall(r'\s+', line)
    return names, gaps

# rename scans so the date comes first
for f in *.png; do
  d=$(date -r "$f" +%Y%m%d)
  mv "$f" "$d-scan.png"
done
